title: Open Tab: The good, the bad and all the coffee in Evanston Open Tab: The good, the bad and all the coffee in Evanston
text:
There is something quintessentially collegiate about grabbing a drink at a local coffee shop and sitting down to do work.
Evanston is home to dozens of coffee shops, and The Daily traveled to a few of the most popular among Northwestern students to see whether they were favorites for their coffee or their convenience.
I ordered the same drink at each shop — a vanilla iced latte — except at Philz Coffee, but more on that later. I told each stop to use their default milk.
Gallery • 5 Photos
Dashiel Berk/The Daily Northwestern
Baristas made drinks behind the counter at a crowded Colectivo on Thursday.
Colectivo Coffee, 716 Church St.
Located just a few blocks from campus, Colectivo Coffee was the shortest walk I took. When I entered the shop, I felt my anxiety rise as I pushed through the crowd that had formed inside. There wasn’t anywhere for me to sit.
My iced latte was derivative, uninspired and bland, yet also somehow full of flavors I didn’t want. The drink used store-bought syrup, which isn’t what I look for in a coffee shop with such a distinctive vibe.
The cheap-tasting vanilla, ice and milk were all blended before the one barista manning the espresso machine added the shot. The drink then sat untouched for several minutes. By the time I got it, it was watered down.
Newport Coffee House, 622 Davis St.
I had heard good things about Newport Coffee House from my friends, but I was skeptical my matcha-drinking pals could provide solid recommendations for coffee.
The flavor of this coffee was spectacular. It was the most delicious coffee I had ever tasted. The sweetness was spot on, elevating the flavor and tying the whole drink together. It contained the right amount of milk and didn’t feel watered down — which often happens with iced espresso-based drinks.
While the food selection at Newport definitely left something to be desired compared to the other spots on my coffee crawl, it’s the place I recommend if you are trying to get the best cup of joe possible.
Philz Coffee, 1030 Davis St.
I visited Philz for a coffee chat. My friend and I were so fascinated by this place that we spent most of an hour talking about it afterwards.
The menu at Philz doesn’t look like a traditional coffee shop. Instead, you pick your type of coffee bean, based on the flavor notes listed on the board. You then choose the size, hot or cold, milk and sweetness level of the drink.
I ordered the Oatmeal Cookie Cold Brew, and it was fantastic. I could taste the cinnamon throughout the drink, not just at the top, which, in my experience, is quite rare. The coffee was smooth and wasn’t as overpowering as I typically find cold brew.
As someone with a go-to coffee order, the unique menu pushed me to try something new, and I really enjoyed it.
Cupitol Coffee & Eatery, 812 Grove St.
I truly think that Cupitol has the total package. Calling it a coffee shop is definitely a stretch, but I don’t think “restaurant” is much better either.
The shop puts a lot of emphasis on its beverages, while offering quite a large selection of breakfast and lunch options. Starting at 11 a.m., it even serves alcohol.
The coffee here is good. I found the latte a bit more milk-based than the others, but I also enjoyed the vanilla flavoring. One nice touch is that your coffee comes in a mason jar if you order “for here.” I found that the unique dishware elevated the experience.
Conclusion
Beyond Colectivo, I really enjoyed all the spots on my coffee tour around Evanston, and will visit my top three again. The next time you take a first sip of a new drink, think about the combinations and flavors at work. Then look around and appreciate all the choices that went into creating the atmosphere that you’re experiencing. Cheers!
